articles.title: Newscast - Will Reform Have To Give Their Mega Donations Back? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: The government is trying to change the law but will it affect Reform’s record donations?
articles.body: After Reform’s £72 million record donations, we’re looking at whether they’ll be allowed to keep the money. Legislation is going through Parliament that could limit the amount of money foreign donors can give, and be applied restrospectively, but Robert Jenrick has said the recent donations were "entirely in line with the law". articles.title: Andy Burnham among Great North Run 2026 finishers
articles.summary: This year's event sees 63,000 people take on the half marathon - including the prime minister.
articles.body:
The Great North Run (GNR) returned to Tyneside this weekend, with 63,000 runners taking part in the world's biggest half marathon - including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

England star and Newcastle captain Dan Burn rang the starter's bell, with famous faces including football personality Chris Kamara and fitness coach Joe Wicks taking on the challenge.

The 13.1-mile (21km) event saw runners and wheelchair users race from Newcastle through Gateshead and South Tyneside, before finishing in South Shields.

Britons David Weir and Melanie Woods won the men's and women's elite wheelchair races respectively. Brigid Kosgei won the elite women's contest and Zouhair Talbi won the men's race.

The half marathon is in its 45th year and raises about £25m for charity each time.

Tens of thousands of people lined the route on the very warm, sunny day.

Runners were treated to a Red Arrows flyover above the Tyne Bridge at the start and again at the end of the route on The Leas in South Shields.

The prime minister said he was "very happy" with his finish time of under two hours - 01.57 - and was raising money for North East charity Changing Lives, which he visited last month to launch a national drive to end rough sleeping.

"You see the causes people are running for, all pulling together for the bigger cause," Burnham said. "It's just a day that reminds you how good this country is when it's together like this.

"This part of the world, it doesn't half shine on a day like this. The warmth of the people comes out - the people in the race with you, the people on the sidelines."

As always, runners donned a variety of costumes in the bid to raise funds for good causes. Among them were nuns, horses and a pair of ovaries.

The Tyne Bridge is undergoing a major restoration project so large parts of it were covered in scaffolding.

Several planned road closures were in place across the day, meanwhile a burst water main at the roundabout near the A189 Redheugh Bridge caused traffic disruption around Gatehead.

Saturday's Mini and Junior events on Newcastle's Quayside saw 13,000 young people take on courses ranging from 50m (164ft) to 4km (2.5 miles).

Gladiators Alex Gray (Apollo), Emily Steel (Dynamite) and Matty Campbell (Bionic) rang Saturday's starters' bell alongside GNR mascot Tyney the Tortoise.

According to organisers, this year's Mini and Junior events were the biggest in its 40-year history.

They gave youngsters "the chance to experience their own Great North Run moment - creating memories, soaking up the atmosphere and, for many, getting a taste of what the main event feels like", they added.

The 2026 medal was designed by local artist Alex Mulholland - known as Mul - and features the Tyne Bridge.

"The design celebrates the stories behind each runner, and the incredible causes that inspire so many people to take on the event," he said.

articles.title: Conheça os cuidados com alimentos de animais em Parque Ecológico em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Referência internacional na preservação e na reprodução de animais silvestres na América do Sul, o Parque Ecológico de São Carlos (SP) completou 50 anos na quarta-feira (8).
articles.summary: Referência internacional na preservação e na reprodução de animais silvestres na América do Sul, o Parque Ecológico de São Carlos completou 50 anos na quarta-feira (8).
articles.body:
Referência internacional na preservação e na reprodução de animais silvestres na América do Sul, o Parque Ecológico de São Carlos completou 50 anos na quarta-feira (8). Os cozinheiros preparam mais de 100 quilos de alimentos diariamente para os animais.

Cada refeição servida aos animais do Parque Ecológico carrega um gesto de afeto e muita dedicação, que começa antes do dia clarear. A chefe do Cuidado Animal Maria de Jesus Pereira Miranda explicou que o cardápio é elaborado pelo setor de nutrição e leva em conta a espécie de cada animal.

"No inverno, eles ganham um tipo de alimento que fornece mais energia, mais calor. No verão, um alimento que também resfria o corpo deles", complementou Maria.

O setor de Nutrição do Parque Ecológico evoluiu nos últimos anos e os ingredientes passaram a ser cuidadosamente escolhidos para manter a imunidade dos animais em dia, além de estimular os comportamentos naturais de cada espécie.

50 kg de hortifrtis, 10 kg de carne e 75 kg de ração: conheça os cuidados com a alimentação dos animais em Parque Ecológico de São Carlos — Foto: EPTV/Reprodução

O Parque Ecológico abriga uma cozinha industrial, onde são preparados, todos os dias, 50 quilos de hortifrútis, 10 quilos de carne e 75 quilos de ração, que envolvem um trabalho minucioso de corte e pesagem.

O cozinheiro Valdecir Donizette Baldan contou que eles entram no trabalho às 6h. "A gente tem o apoio de uma equipe técnica que prepara a dieta de cada animal e a gente segue essa dieta rigorosa com pesos e medidas para que cada animal seja atendido de acordo com a sua necessidade".

A equipe de cozinheiros não trabalha com receita única. Cada bandeja que sai da cozinha industrial tem um destino certo, com hora marcada e peso exato. Do menor pássaro até o maior carnívoro, a principal preocupação é a qualidade dos alimentos para garantir a longevidade dos animais.

50 kg de hortifrutis, 10 kg de carne e 75 kg de ração: conheça os cuidados com a alimentação dos animais em Parque Ecológico de São Carlos — Foto: EPTV/Reprodução

Cada detalhe é importante: o jeito de cortar os alimentos, a textura e até a forma de apresentação servem como estímulo para que o animal mantenha o comportamento que teria na natureza.

O cozinheiro Kaian Goulart Santos explicou que os alimentos são cortados pensando na forma como o tratador conseguirá oferecê-los ao animal. Para os micos, por exemplo, as frutas são cortadas em formatos pequenos, semelhantes ao tamanho das mãozinhas.

Quem está na cozinha também fica de olho no clima, já que a alimentação dos animais muda de acordo com a temperatura. "A gente está acompanhando o ano inteiro o clima com os bichos. O clima mudou, vai mudar alguma coisa para melhorar para eles", disse Kaian.

50 kg de hortifrútis, 10 kg de carne e 75 kg de ração: conheça os cuidados com a alimentação dos animais em Parque Ecológico de São Carlos — Foto: EPTV/Reprodução

Assim que a alimentação fica pronta, ela é transportada para, depois, ser distribuída nos recintos. Maria afirmou que, com o passar dos anos, percebe que os animais estão bem mais cuidados devido à alimentação.

"Tudo sai daqui, tudo é daqui. Se a cozinha parar, o parque para também", disse a chefe do Cuidado Animal.

Valdecir relembrou que os animais foram privados da liberdade, mas que a equipe se dedica a eles há 50 anos. "A gente aqui tem esse compromisso de favorecer, de fornecer a eles o melhor possível. Então, a gente trabalha aqui com muito carinho, com muita dedicação".

articles.title: Fumaça em Manaus: Qualidade do ar atinge nível péssimo em bairros | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados do Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental, da UEA, apontaram que a qualidade do ar chegou a níveis considerados péssimos em bairros como Morro da Liberdade, Aparecida e Cachoeirinha por volta de 1h.
articles.summary: A fumaça em Manaus atingiu níveis péssimos de qualidade do ar em diversos bairros neste domingo, com alertas da Defesa Civil para riscos à saúde.
articles.body:
Manaus amanhece com fumaça forte e qualidade do ar chega a nível ‘péssimo’ em bairros. — Foto: Reprodução

Manaus voltou a registrar forte presença de fumaça na madrugada deste domingo (13). Moradores de diferentes áreas da cidade relataram a presença intensa do material no ar, principalmente nas primeiras horas do dia.

Dados do Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva), da Universidade do Estado do Amazonas ( UEA ), apontaram que a qualidade do ar chegou a níveis considerados péssimos em bairros como Morro da Liberdade, Aparecida e Cachoeirinha por volta de 1h.

Na Zona Oeste de Manaus, o sistema de monitoramento classificou a qualidade do ar como muito ruim no mesmo período. Até a publicação desta reportagem, não havia informações sobre o que pode ter causado a nuvem de fumaça .

🔎 A qualidade do ar é considerada boa quando a concentração de partículas fica entre 0 e 25 microgramas por metro cúbico (µg/m³) .

Por volta das 9h30, a qualidade do ar já havia melhorado e apresentava boas condições em toda a região da capital.

Já os dados do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais ( Inpe ) indicavam, durante a manhã, concentração de 25,73 microgramas por metro cúbico de material particulado fino (PM2,5), índice classificado como moderado.

A situação ocorre quatro dias após Manaus amanhecer novamente encoberta por fumaça . Na quarta-feira (9), sensores do Selva chegaram a registrar 118 microgramas por metro cúbico de partículas durante a madrugada em alguns pontos da cidade, nível considerado muito ruim .

Na ocasião, pesquisadores e órgãos públicos apontaram que a fumaça poderia estar relacionada a queimadas em diferentes áreas da Amazônia e ao transporte do material por ventos em baixos níveis da atmosfera.

classificação da qualidade do ar varia de acordo com a concentração de partículas presentes na atmosfera. Quanto maior a quantidade de material particulado fino, maior o risco de impactos à saúde, especialmente para pessoas mais sensíveis.

Níveis de poluição do ar em Manaus por volta de 1h deste domingo (13) — Foto: Reprodução/Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva)

Com a piora da qualidade do ar, a orientação da Defesa Civil é reduzir a exposição prolongada à fumaça e evitar atividades físicas intensas ao ar livre nos períodos de maior concentração de partículas .

A recomendação também é manter-se hidratado e acompanhar as atualizações sobre a qualidade do ar e as condições meteorológicas.

A Defesa Civil informou que continua monitorando a situação ao longo desta quarta-feira e que novas informações devem ser divulgadas caso haja mudança significativa no cenário.

Em situações de risco, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil pelo telefone 199.

articles.title: Agrotóxicos em Itapetininga: projeto orienta uso e descarte correto | G1
articles.standfirst: Atividades gratuitas serão realizadas na quarta-feira (16) e quinta-feira (17) e também haverá campanha para recolher embalagens vazias e produtos vencidos.
articles.summary: Ação da Defesa Agropecuária em Itapetininga oferece treinamento gratuito e coleta de embalagens e agrotóxicos vencidos nesta quarta e quinta-feira.
articles.body:
Sindicato Rural de Itapetininga — Foto: Divulgação

Um projeto que orienta produtores sobre o uso, armazenamento e descarte correto de agrotóxicos será realizado na quarta-feira (16) e quinta-feira (17) em Itapetininga (SP).

As atividades são gratuitas e fazem parte do projeto “Produzindo Alimento Seguro”, da Defesa Agropecuária do estado de São Paulo. As inscrições para as atividades devem ser feitas pelo site .

A programação é voltada principalmente para pequenos e médios produtores, responsáveis técnicos e jovens. Também haverá uma campanha para receber embalagens vazias e agrotóxicos impróprios para uso, como produtos vencidos ou que ainda tenham sobras.

Conforme a Defesa Agropecuária, na quarta-feira, as atividades começam às 9h, no Sindicato Rural de Itapetininga. Pela manhã, as palestras serão destinadas a responsáveis técnicos e vão abordar temas como a prescrição de agrotóxicos, responsabilidade técnica e agricultura regenerativa.

À tarde, o conteúdo será direcionado aos produtores. Entre os assuntos estão os cuidados na compra e no uso de agrotóxicos, formas corretas de armazenamento e boas práticas com bioinsumos.

Já na quinta-feira, a partir das 8h30, o Centro de Apoio ao Adolescente receberá atividades voltadas ao público jovem. Os participantes vão conhecer ações da Defesa Agropecuária e o funcionamento do programa Sistema Campo Limpo, responsável pela destinação de embalagens vazias de defensivos agrícolas.

Depois, os participantes farão uma visita técnica ao posto da Associação dos Distribuidores de Insumos Agrícolas (Adiaesp).

Também na manhã de quinta-feira, o posto da Adiaesp fará uma campanha especial para receber embalagens vazias de agrotóxicos e produtos impróprios para uso.

A iniciativa foi criada pela Defesa Agropecuária a partir de dados do Programa Estadual de Análise de Resíduos de Agrotóxicos e Afins de Uso Agrícola em Produtos de Origem Vegetal (PEARA-POV).

Segundo o último relatório do programa, divulgado em março deste ano, 75,4% das lavouras paulistas analisadas apresentaram uso correto de agrotóxicos. As culturas de amendoim, cebola e feijão tiveram 100% de conformidade nas análises.

De acordo com a Defesa Agropecuária, os dados são utilizados para orientar ações de fiscalização e educação sobre o uso dos produtos, com o objetivo de reduzir riscos à saúde e ao meio ambiente e contribuir para a produção de alimentos seguros.

articles.title: Rio Ribeira transborda e Defesa Civil faz alerta no Vale do Ribeira | G1
articles.standfirst: Nível do Rio cresceu 5,6 metros desde quinta-feira (10), em Eldorado (SP), e deve seguir em elevação. Cheia fez 60 pessoas irem para abrigos e deixou outras 60 famílias ilhadas em Ribeira (SP) neste sábado (12).
articles.summary: Rio Ribeira atinge 7,5 metros acima da média, isola famílias e mobiliza a Defesa Civil em cidades do Vale do Ribeira após fortes chuvas na região.
articles.body:
Rio Ribeira de Iguape, em Eldorado, neste sábado (12). — Foto: Luiz Momisso

O nível das águas do Rio Ribeira de Iguape , que corta os municípios do Vale do Ribeira , segue com tendência de elevação em diversos pontos, segundo informou a Defesa Civil Estadual, na manhã deste domingo (13). Ainda segundo a pasta, as áreas suscetíveis a inundações e alagamentos estão em condição de alerta. O órgão disse que segue monitorando as condições hidrológicas da região.

A cheia do Rio Ribeira fez com que cerca de 60 pessoas precisassem deixar as suas residências para abrigos municipais e deixou outras 60 famílias ilhadas em Ribeira (SP) , por conta da interdição de rodovias, na tarde deste sábado (12).

Segundo a Prefeitura de Ribeira, o nível do rio subiu 7,5 metros acima da média, que não foi informada. Na quinta-feira (10), o nível do Rio estava em 4,04 metros no município, e chegou a 7,17 na madrugada deste domingo (13).

Em Sete Barras, o transbordamento do Rio Ribeira de Iguape inundou vias e propriedades rurais, afetando 50 moradias. Em Eldorado (SP), foi necessária a retirada preventiva de 173 pessoas que residem na área urbana, totalizando 54 famílias, por conta do aumento do nível do rio.

De acordo com a Defesa Civil de Eldorado, o nível do Rio cresceu 5,6 metros desde quinta-feira (10) e chegou a 9,18 metros neste domingo (13). O prefeito da cidade, Noel Castelo (Solidariedade), destacou que o município trabalha com uma margem de cheia de até 12 metros.

“Nós queremos pecar pelo excesso do que pecar por omissão”, disse o prefeito. Ele também pontuou que, em outras ocasiões, houve relatos de residências sendo invadidas pelas águas do Rio quando o nível chegou a mais de 9 metros.

Ainda conforme a Defesa Civil, foi enviada ajuda humanitária para a região, com mais 100 cestas básicas, 50 colchões, 50 cobertores, 50 kits dormitório, 100 kits de higiene, 100 kits de limpeza, um palete de água potável, três rolos de lona plástica e cinco rolos de fita de isolamento.

"Este envio se soma aos mais de 2 mil itens que já tinham sido enviados pela própria Defesa Civil e também pelo Fundo Social de São Paulo às cidades de Avaré, Piedade, Sumaré, Juquitiba, Monte Mor, Ibiúna e Sete Barras", disse a pasta, destancando que uma balsa inflável também foi destinada a região

O prefeito Noel destacou que as cheias do Rio possuem relação com as fortes chuvas registradas no Estado de São Paulo (SP) e Paraná (PR). Ele disse que o nível do Rio sofre forte influência da represa do rio Capivari, localizada em Campina Grande do Sul.

Noel também destacou que, na quinta-feira (10), a represa administrada pela Companhia Paranaense de Energia (Copel) trabalhava com uma vazão de 27 mil litros de água por segundo, que chega ao Rio Ribeira após passar pelos rios Capivari e Pardo.

Noel destacou, no entanto, que a vazão foi ampliada para cerca de 140 mil litros de água devido a represa atingir 88% de armazenamento nesta quinta (10). Por conta disso, ele pediu para que moradores de áreas mais baixas procurem abrigo em locais elevados.

“Nós não estamos querendo criar pânico em ninguém, podem ter certeza disso. Mas nós também não queremos deixar que as coisas aconteçam e a gente não tenha pernas para estar atendendo vocês”, disse.

articles.title: Inmet emite alerta de tempestade para Sul do Rio e Costa Verde | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidades podem esperar chuvas entre 20 e 30 mm/h ou até 50 mm/dia, ventos intensos entre 40 a 60 km/h, e queda de granizo.
articles.summary: O alerta de tempestade no Sul do Rio e Costa Verde prevê chuvas de até 50 mm/dia, ventos intensos e queda de granizo em 24 municípios da região.
articles.body:
Inmet emite alerta de declínio de temperatura para cidades do Sul do Rio e Costa Verde — Foto: Divulgação/

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) divulgou neste domingo (13), um alerta amarelo, que significa perigo potencial, de tempestade para as 24 cidades do Sul do Rio e Costa Verde. O aviso começou às 0h e vai até às 23h59.

O aviso é válido para as cidades de Angra dos Reis (RJ), Barra do Piraí (RJ), Barra Mansa (RJ), Engenheiro Paulo de Frontin (RJ), Itatiaia (RJ), Comendador Levy Gasparian (RJ), Mendes (RJ), Miguel Pereira (RJ), Paracambi (RJ), Paraíba do Sul (RJ), Paraty (RJ), Paty do Alferes (RJ), Pinheiral (RJ), Piraí (RJ), Porto Real (RJ), Quatis (RJ), Resende (RJ), Rio Claro (RJ), Rio das Flores (RJ), Sapucaia (RJ), Três Rios (RJ), Valença (RJ), Vassouras (RJ) e Volta Redonda (RJ).

Segundo o Instituto, as cidades podem registrar chuvas entre 20 e 30 mm/h ou até 50 mm/dia, ventos intensos que podem variar entre 40 a 60 km/h, e queda de granizo. Além do baixo risco de corte de energia elétrica, estragos em plantações, queda de galhos de árvores e de alagamentos.

De acordo com o Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden), há registros de chuvas fracas na região da Costa Verde.

articles.title: O que novo presidente da Colômbia pretende com polêmicas imagens caminhando entre cadáveres | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens de Espriella entre corpos de supostos guerrilheiros reforçam discurso linha-dura contra o crime e provocam críticas na Colômbia.
articles.summary: Imagens de Espriella entre corpos de supostos guerrilheiros reforçam discurso linha-dura contra o crime e provocam críticas na Colômbia.
articles.body:
Durante sua campanha eleitoral, o presidente colombiano Abelardo de la Espriella prometeu uma postura firme contra o crime.

Essas promessas foram consideradas por vários analistas como um dos fatores que contribuíram para a vitória dele nas eleições de junho.

Espriella caminhando entre os corpos de supostos guerrilheiros — Foto: Reprodução Redes Sociais

Mas imagens compartilhadas por Espriella, nas quais ele aparece caminhando entre os corpos de supostos guerrilheiros mortos em uma operação militar, geraram debate e fortes críticas.

O vídeo causou controvérsia em uma nação traumatizada por décadas de conflito armado e atrocidades cometidas tanto por insurgentes quanto por membros do exército e paramilitares.

Na última quinta-feira (10/09), um juiz em Bogotá ordenou que o presidente ocultasse temporariamente essas publicações, segundo a agência de notícias AFP, que obteve o documento.

Uma das pessoas que condenaram essas imagens foi a Defensora do Povo (cargo ligado ao Ministério Público da Colômbia), Iris Marín.

"O Estado e o Governo não podem competir para ver quem consegue ser o mais cruel", disse ela na rede social X.

"Mesmo em tempos de guerra, há limites, e a dignidade humana não desaparece com a morte. As imagens e os símbolos do poder público também importam."

É precisamente no que essas imagens e símbolos comunicam que pode estar o que Espriella busca com sua estratégia de segurança.

O presidente divulgou um primeiro vídeo após uma operação das forças militares colombianas em Guaviare, na qual 23 supostos membros dissidentes das Farc (Forças Armadas Revolucionárias da Colômbia) e dois menores de idade foram mortos.

Desde o início de seu governo, Espriella tem prometido impulsionar as forças militares do país — Foto: Raul Arboleda/AFP via Getty Images

O momento em que ele aparece caminhando entre os cadáveres faz parte de um vídeo mais longo, com pouco mais de sete minutos, no qual ele detalha as operações militares e informações sobre os insurgentes capturados e mortos.

Dois dias depois, Espriella publicou novas imagens nas quais aparece perto de cadáveres após uma operação em La Guajira, no norte do país, na qual Naín Andrés Pérez Toncel (vulgo Bendito Menor), sua companheira Angélica Tarazona (vulgo La Bebecita) e outras duas pessoas foram mortas.

"Mostrar isso transmite uma mensagem de força e intimidação", afirma o cientista político Carlos Cortés.

O analista vê nas imagens uma coerência com a postura linha-dura que Espriella disse que adotaria em relação à segurança.

O atual presidente se distancia, assim, da estratégia de seu antecessor, Gustavo Petro, que optou por negociar com os grupos armados para pôr fim ao conflito.

Elizabeth Dickinson, analista do International Crisis Group, concorda que o presidente colombiano busca "enfatizar uma narrativa ofensiva".

"As imagens mostram o controle do Estado sobre os criminosos", destaca a especialista.

Segundo pesquisas de opinião, para uma parcela significativa dos colombianos, a principal preocupação está na segurança e na ordem pública.

Desde o lançamento de sua campanha presidencial, Espriella tem aparecido em eventos públicos vestindo um colete à prova de balas, atrás de púlpitos blindados e entoando slogans contra o que ele chama de "narcoterrorismo".

Catalina Suárez, estrategista política, acredita que essa performance nunca foi acidental: "Ele usa símbolos para mostrar que não se intimida".

Sua caminhada entre cadáveres reforça a imagem de homem forte com a qual venceu a eleição e que agora quer manter no governo.

Trecho de outro vídeo compartilhado pelo governo de Espriella — Foto: Reprodução/ Gobierno de Colombia

Muitos de seus apoiadores ficaram satisfeitos com as imagens, como demonstram inúmeras mensagens que o presidente recebeu nas redes sociais.

Mas muitos outros cidadãos e figuras da oposição as criticaram duramente.

"Estamos testemunhando uma necrofilia midiática", disse a senadora María José Pizarro, do Pacto Histórico, partido de Petro.

Claudia López, ex-prefeita de Bogotá e ex-candidata à presidência, abordou a controvérsia, afirmando que "o autoritarismo mafioso não respeita nem a vida nem a morte".

O debate ganhou outra dimensão quando a Defensora do Povo se manifestou, pedindo que o Estado não competisse para demonstrar crueldade.

Espriella se elegeu com um discurso linha-dura contra o crime — Foto: Raul Arbolerda/ APF via Getty Images

A posição dela foi contestada pelo ministro do Interior, Rodrigo Lara Restrepo — filho de Rodrigo Lara Bonilla, ministro da Justiça morto a tiros em um crime atribuído ao Cartel de Medellín em tempos de Pablo Escobar.

"Lamentamos (...) o que consideramos um triste erro: equiparar o Estado a gangues narcoterroristas, como se estivessem competindo em crueldade (...) O Estado cumpre um dever constitucional de combater criminosos que perpetram o terror", escreveu o ministro.

Dickinson afirmou que esse tipo de demonstração de autoridade não é novidade na Colômbia.

"Durante a luta contra Escobar e os cartéis, imagens circularam. A famosa foto de Escobar morto perto de policiais foi amplamente divulgada."

Em El Salvador, sob o comando de Bukele, imagens de supostos membros de gangues na prisão transmitem forte mensagem de submissão do crime ao Estado — Foto: Marvin Recinos / AFP Via Getty Images

A demonstração de autoridade e o uso da força são respostas recorrentes de governos nas Américas a problemas de segurança.

O presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, frequentemente exibe imagens de supostos membros de gangues presos e subjugados.

O presidente americano Donald Trump também compartilhou vídeos de ataques de militares americanos contra embarcações supostamente ligadas ao narcotráfico em águas do Caribe e do Pacífico.

"A campanha dos EUA, na qual eles essencialmente executam extrajudicialmente supostos traficantes de drogas, abre caminho, acredito, para outros comportamentos que estão se repetindo na região", afirma Dickinson.

"Se os EUA se comportam dessa maneira, rebaixam os padrões para o resto dos países."

No caso da Colômbia, onde conflitos armados ferem a nação há mais de 60 anos, Dickinson alerta para o outro lado da demonstração de poder.

"Nas comunidades afetadas pelo conflito, as imagens de Espriella são arrepiantes porque transmitem uma mensagem que enfatiza o número de mortos", destaca.

A analista lembra que amplificar essa mensagem já levou, no passado, à morte de civis inocentes e ao aumento da violência estatal.

"Não estou dizendo que isso esteja acontecendo agora, mas poderia ter o mesmo impacto no contexto colombiano", esclarece.

articles.title: Crianças buscam Centro de Valorização da Vida para denunciar bullying | G1
articles.standfirst: Coordenador do CVV de São José do Rio Preto (SP) registrou aumento de jovens de 10 a 17 anos que procuram o serviço motivados por bullying, pressão das redes sociais e isolamento familiar.
articles.summary: O CVV de Rio Preto alerta para o aumento de atendimentos a jovens de 10 a 17 anos e abre vagas para novos voluntários ajudarem no combate ao bullying.
articles.body:
O Centro de Valorização da Vida (CVV) de São José do Rio Preto (SP) registrou um aumento na procura por atendimento entre crianças e adolescentes de 10 a 17 anos.

De janeiro a agosto deste ano, o local realizou cerca de 32 mil atendimentos, mantendo uma média mensal de 3 mil a 3,5 mil ligações. Durante o mês de setembro, segundo a associação, a expectativa é de atingir a marca de 5 mil chamadas. Veja abaixo como se tornar um voluntário.

João trabalha como voluntário no CVV em Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: João/Arquivo pessoal

Em entrevista à TV TEM , o coordenador do CVV, Francisco Garcia, informou que o público infanto-juvenil tem enfrentado sobrecargas emocionais precoces.

A situação acende um alerta para a saúde mental dos mais jovens, que buscam o serviço gratuito de escuta para relatar crises de ansiedade, depressão, bullying, automutilação e o distanciamento afetivo dos pais.

"Essas crianças que ligam para o CVV buscando ajuda trazem para nós relatos de crise dentro de casa: crise financeira, crise de aceitação de si mesmo, bullying. A correria do dia a dia acaba fazendo com que essas crianças se sintam sozinhas. Hoje, percebemos que temos crianças vivendo problemas de adultos", avalia o coordenador.

No entanto, apesar da alta procura, a estrutura atual da entidade opera no limite de sua capacidade. Ainda segundo Francisco, o CVV conta com 21 voluntários ativos em Rio Preto . Para que o atendimento não seja interrompido e para suprir a demanda da região, seriam necessárias 56 pessoas.

Devido ao baixo número de atendentes, estima-se que 25% das ligações destinadas ao posto acabam não sendo finalizadas imediatamente, caindo em uma fila de espera nacional.

Para tentar expandir a equipe de atendimento, o CVV de Rio Preto está com inscrições abertas para novos voluntários. O trabalho não é remunerado, realizado de forma anônima, sigilosa e sem julgamentos morais ou religiosos.

O que faz: realiza atendimento presencial, telefônico (188), via chat ou e-mail, oferecendo escuta ativa e empática a quem passa por sofrimento emocional;

Dedicação exigida : plantões semanais de aproximadamente 4 horas;

Requisitos: ter no mínimo 18 anos completos e disponibilidade para realizar o curso preparatório gratuito oferecido pela instituição.

articles.summary: As notícias do g1 Grande Minas destacam o alerta de tempestade do Inmet e os desdobramentos de acidentes fatais que impactaram a região nos últimos sete dias.
articles.body:
O g1 Grande Minas reúne as cinco notícias mais lidas nos últimos sete dias para você ficar por dentro dos assuntos que mais chamaram a atenção dos internautas. Um alerta de tempestade emitido pelo Inmet, a morte de uma criança atingida por um muro em São Francisco e o atropelamento de uma mulher por um carro conduzido pela esposa do prefeito de Pintópolis estão entre os assuntos mais buscados pelos internautas.

INMET emite alerta de 'tempestade' para 129 cidades do Norte, Centro e Noroeste de MG

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu nesta semana um alerta amarelo de “tempestade” para 129 cidades das regiões Norte, Centro e Noroeste de Minas Gerais

O aviso, classificado como “Perigo potencial”, indica previsão de chuva entre 20 e 30 mm por hora ou 50 mm por dia, com ventos intensos (40 a 60km/h) e queda de granizo.

Investigado por esquema de cultivo de maconha em MG é preso na BA; 5 plantações já foram descobertas

Plantação descoberta tem 40 mil pés de maconha, segundo a polícia — Foto: Polícia Civil

Durante as investigações, cerca de sete toneladas da droga foram encontradas em cinco locais e 12 pessoas foram detidas.

De acordo com a Polícia Civil de Minas Gerais (PCMG), o homem é apontado como um dos operadores do negócio. O mandado de prisão preventiva foi expedido pela Comarca de Araçuaí, no Vale do Jequitinhonha.

Adolescente morre após carro bater em carreta durante ultrapassagem na BR-135

Adolescente morre após carro bater em carreta durante ultrapassagem na BR-135, em Bocaiuva — Foto: Polícia Militar Rodoviária

Um adolescente de 14 anos morreu após o carro em que estava bater contra uma carreta na BR-135, em Bocaiuva, no Norte de Minas. Segundo a Polícia, o motorista do carro, avô do adolescente, tentava fazer uma ultrapassagem quando o acidente aconteceu.

O caso foi registrado por volta das 8h05, no km 422 da rodovia, no sentido Sul. De acordo com a Ecovias Norte Minas, concessionária responsável pelo trecho, houve uma colisão transversal entre os veículos.

'Tá sem chão', diz tio sobre mãe de menino que morreu ao ser atingido por parede em São Francisco

Rafael Raposo de Almeida — Foto: Redes sociais

O tio de Rafael Raposo de Almeida, Gleison Queiroz disse que a família está profundamente abalada com a morte do garoto de três anos . O menino foi atingido por uma parede do imóvel vizinho enquanto brincava na casa da bisavó, em São Francisco. O irmão gêmeo também se feriu.

“A mãe tá sem chão, não aguenta mais tanta dor”, disse Gleisson.

Rafael e o irmão foram socorridos com a ajuda de vizinhos, que providenciaram o encaminhamento das crianças para o hospital. Segundo a Defesa Civil Municipal, a parede que caiu estava fora do padrão.

Filho cobra justiça após mãe ser atropelada por esposa de prefeito: 'Que pague pelo que fez'

O filho de Maria Evanilde Vieira Rosa, de 63 anos, que morreu após ser atropelada em São Francisco, disse que o desejo da família é que a motorista seja punida . O prefeito de Pintópolis, cidade vizinha, confirmou que a esposa dele, Josiane Ruas, era quem dirigia o veículo que atingiu a idosa.

"Nosso desejo é por justiça, que ela pague pelo que fez e que sirva de exemplo para crimes desse mesmo tipo", disse José Adailson Vieira dos Santoa.

Um vídeo (veja acima) mostra o momento em que o atropelamento ocorreu. Testemunhas contaram que a motorista transitava em alta velocidade. Ela deixou o local sem prestar socorro.

articles.title: ‘Body lay on road for 2.5 hours’: Blinkit delivery worker killed as bike crashes into divider in Sonipat
articles.summary: SONIPAT: A 25-year-old man was killed and two of his friends sustained injuries after their motorcycle crashed into a road divider on Murthal Road in .
articles.body: SONIPAT: A 25-year-old man was killed and two of his friends sustained injuries after their motorcycle crashed into a road divider on Murthal Road in Sonipat early Sunday morning.The deceased, identified as Sumit, was riding the motorcycle when it lost control following the collision with the divider, causing all three riders to fall onto the road.Sumit, a resident of Sandal Kalan village, sustained critical injuries and died at the spot. His companions, Prince and Sahil, were injured in the accident and were subsequently taken to Sonipat Civil Hospital.Prince’s condition was reported to be serious, following which doctors referred him to Rohtak PGI for further treatment. Sahil was treated at Sonipat Civil Hospital.According to police, the accident occurred at around 5am on Sunday. The motorcycle reportedly rammed into a divider on Murthal Road and went out of control. All three men fell onto the road following the impact.Sumit, who was riding the motorcycle, suffered severe injuries and succumbed at the spot.Police received information about the accident through Dial-112 at around 6:44am.A police team subsequently reached the spot and inspected the accident site.According to information available, Sumit, Prince and Sahil were all working as delivery workers for Blinkit.People familiar with their work said Sumit usually worked the night shift and would generally return home at around 8am after completing his duty.On Sunday too, he was reportedly on his way home after completing his night shift when the accident occurred on Murthal Road.Another account concerning the incident says that the three friends were returning after a party. Since the accounts regarding where they were coming from differ, the exact circumstances immediately preceding the accident would have to be established through the police inquiry.Sumit was a resident of Sandal Kalan village in Sonipat. He was married and is survived by his wife and a child aged around two to three years, according to the information available.The news of his death plunged the family into grief. Police informed his relatives and initiated the necessary proceedings.Sumit’s body was sent to the Civil Hospital for a post-mortem examination. After the procedure was completed, the body was handed over to his family.Following the accident, the injured Prince and Sahil were taken to Sonipat Civil Hospital.Doctors referred Prince to Rohtak PGI after assessing his condition as serious, while Sahil continued to receive treatment at the Civil Hospital in Sonipat.There was also a claim that Prince tested positive for alcohol. However, police have not officially confirmed the claim, and it should therefore be treated as an allegation or reported information rather than an established fact.Bystanders Allege Body Remained on Road for Nearly 2.5 HoursThe accident also raised questions among people who were present at the scene regarding the response to the incident.According to eyewitnesses, local commuters stepped in to assist the injured. One of the injured men was reportedly taken to hospital by a passer-by in his own vehicle, while the other was transported by ambulance.Bystanders have alleged that Sumit’s body remained at the accident site for nearly two-and-a-half hours. They further claimed that two or three ambulances passed through the area during this period but did not stop at the spot, allegedly citing the fact that it was a police case.The allegations have not been independently verified, and police have not officially confirmed them.Bystanders said that prompt medical assistance and emergency response could potentially have made a difference to the situation. However, whether the delay occurred and whether it had any bearing on the outcome would be determined only through an official inquiry.The incident falls under the jurisdiction of Sector 27 police station in Sonipat.SHO Inspector Savit Kumar said that the police had completed the required proceedings following the accident. He said Sumit’s body was subjected to a post-mortem examination and was subsequently handed over to his family.According to the SHO, no action has been initiated against anyone in connection with the accident, as the motorcycle had collided with the road divider.Inspector Savit Kumar said the available findings indicated that the motorcycle struck the divider and that there was no basis for action against another person or vehicle.The family subsequently performed Sumit’s last rites in his village.After receiving the emergency call, the police team reached the spot and inspected the scene. The circumstances surrounding the crash were examined as part of the proceedings.Police are looking into the circumstances in which the motorcycle collided with the divider and the events immediately preceding the accident.The information regarding the emergency call states that police were alerted through Dial-112 at around 6:44am, following which officers reached the location.The body was taken into police custody for the post-mortem examination and was later handed over to the family after completion of the formalities.The allegations made by bystanders regarding the time taken to remove Sumit’s body and the alleged response of ambulances have also become part of the discussion surrounding the accident.However, these remain claims made by eyewitnesses, and there has been no official confirmation of the allegations.The Sector 27 police, meanwhile, have maintained that the motorcycle crashed into the divider and that no other person or vehicle was found to be responsible, leaving no grounds for action against anyone.The precise sequence of events following the accident, including the timing of emergency assistance and the removal of the body, would need to be established on the basis of official records and investigation.Sumit was only 25 years old and worked as a delivery executive to support his family. articles.title: BRICS summit 2026: What are the key takeaways?
articles.summary: The 11-nation bloc avoids condemning the US-Israel war on Iran, showing the divisions among the members.
articles.body:
Leaders of the BRICS group of nations unanimously adopted a joint declaration on the first day of the two-day summit in the Indian capital, New Delhi, despite divisions among members over the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

The New Delhi Declaration, adopted on Saturday, called for restraint in the Middle East but avoided condemning the US-Israeli strikes or Iran’s targeting of Gulf countries in the region. It also criticised the global trade war without naming the United States.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, were among the leaders attending the gathering of the 11-member bloc in New Delhi at a time of global upheaval caused by the US-Israel war on Iran, Trump’s tariff war and the US’s unilateral decisions to promote its foreign policy.

Al Jazeera’s Um-e-Kulsoom Shariff, reporting from New Delhi, said the group “steered clear” of naming any countries, even on the issue of wide-ranging US tariffs. “We’ve seen BRICS countries who have been targeted, be it India, Russia, China, or any other, but they have stayed clear,” she reported.

“While they said unilateral tariffs are condemned and they work against international law, they have not named the US. So India had to keep in mind that it has bilateral trade relations with other countries, and so do others.”

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said BRICS had reached a “coming of age” moment and called on the Global South to become a “rule-shaper” rather than simply accept rules set elsewhere.

Here are key takeaways from the declaration from the summit:

BRICS was founded in 2006 by Brazil, Russia, India and China, mainly as an economic forum. South Africa joined the grouping four years later. It has since expanded to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia.

The BRICS nations constitute nearly half the world’s population and account for approximately 40 percent of global gross domestic product (GDP).

The bloc has sought greater influence for developing economies in institutions traditionally dominated by Western powers and has pushed for reforms to bodies, including the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund and the World Trade Organization.

Conveying India’s position, Modi insisted that the bloc should not be interpreted simply as an anti-Western project.

“BRICS is not against anyone,” he said, while arguing that the Global South should play a bigger role in shaping global governance.

The war was one of the biggest tests of whether the expanded BRICS could reach a common position.

Leaders expressed “deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions” in the Middle East and called for “maximum restraint”, while urging countries to avoid actions that could further aggravate the situation. It did not mention the US, Israel, Iran or the Gulf states explicitly.

China’s Xi said in a statement the war “does not serve the common interests of the international community”, and called for a political settlement and a permanent and comprehensive ceasefire.

In May, BRICS foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement amid differences over the war. Iran is a member of BRICS, as is the UAE, which has faced Iranian attacks during the conflict.

Former Indian Foreign Secretary Nirupama Menon Rao said New Delhi scored a “significant diplomatic success” in securing a declaration despite “sharp differences between Iran and the UAE”.

“Consensus was preserved, but only through carefully generalised language. In this, BRICS’s value and its limitation was exposed: it can keep difficult conversations alive and affirm broad principles, but it struggles to assign responsibility or organise collective action when there is the occasional collision of the interests of its members,” she posted on X.

The declaration also raised concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities protected by International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards – language that could be seen as an indirect criticism of US and Israeli attacks on Iranian nuclear sites.

During the 12-day war in 2025, the US bombed three main Iranian nuclear facilities at Natanz, Isfahan and Fordow.

Praveen Donthi, senior analyst at the International Crisis Group, said expectations for the BRICS summit were low due to geopolitical turbulence and clashing strategic interests.

“The members, invested in the success of this non-Western grouping, would be reasonably satisfied with the modest outcome,” he said.

Donthi added that India used its strong ties with all members and worked behind the scenes to release the declaration, overcoming the biggest hurdle: convincing the UAE and Iran, who are on opposite sides of the ongoing conflict.

The Ukraine war remains another source of tension within BRICS, particularly because Russia is a founding member of the group.

The declaration issued a generic call for international disputes to be resolved through “dialogue, consultation, and diplomacy” without mentioning Ukraine.

However, BRICS leaders criticised unilateral sanctions not authorised by the United Nations Security Council.

“We call for the elimination of such unlawful measures, which undermine international law and the principles and purposes of the UN Charter,” the statement said.

The position is significant for Russia, which has faced extensive Western sanctions since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. India, meanwhile, has maintained close relations with Moscow, importing oil from Russia amid disruption to global oil supplies since the US-Israel war on Iran broke out.

Kremlin ⁠spokesman ⁠Dmitry Peskov said on Sunday ⁠that Xi and Modi offered their services for peace talks on Ukraine, and that ⁠Putin welcomed their readiness, state news ⁠agency TASS ⁠reported.

Last year, Trump imposed a 25 percent tariff on Indian goods as a penalty for its purchase of Russian crude. India has since cut down its imports of Russian crude oil.

BRICS adopted much more explicit language on Palestine.

The declaration expressed “firm opposition” to the forced displacement of Palestinians and to attempts to change the geography or demography of the occupied Palestinian territory.

It called for an end to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, unhindered humanitarian access, support for UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, and full UN membership for Palestine.

The bloc also reiterated its support for a two-state solution and the establishment of a sovereign Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders, with occupied East Jerusalem as its capital.

The declaration raised concern over “unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures” that distort trade, while also opposing sanctions imposed without UNSC authorisation.

Washington has imposed tariffs on several BRICS countries, including China, Russia and India, and President Donald Trump has previously described the grouping as “anti-American”. He threatened additional tariffs against countries aligning themselves with it.

Speaking at the summit, Putin accused countries “accustomed to thinking in colonial categories” of using tariffs, sanctions and “brute force” to contain emerging competitors.

At the same time, the bloc called for cooperation to protect global trade, supply chains, energy flows and maritime security as wars disrupt international commerce.

BRICS reiterated its “commitment to strengthening multilateralism and multipolarity”, noting that a multipolar world can expand opportunities for Emerging Markets and Developing Countries (EMDCs) to develop “constructive potential and enjoy universally beneficial, inclusive, sustainable and equitable economic globalisation and cooperation”.

Putin called for greater representation for Asia, Africa and Latin America on the UNSC and argued that the shift towards a multipolar world was being resisted by established powers.

Xi said BRICS countries should help steer the international order towards greater “equity and justice”, while Modi called for the Global South to move from being a rule-taker to a “rule-shaper”.

“We have to transform this pyramid of privilege into a platform of partnership,” Modi told the summit.

Yet India has also sought to distance BRICS from the idea that it exists simply to confront the West. “We are not against anyone; rather, we strive to move forward with the approach of taking everyone along,” he asserted.

articles.title: College football’s chaos era is here: Texas rallies, Oregon falls and Lane Kiffin eyes return to Ole Miss
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin's return to Ole Miss with LSU looms after a chaotic week saw Arch Manning rally Texas past Ohio State and Oklahoma State stun Oregon.
articles.body: If you were waiting for chaos to encompass college football, the second week of the 2026 season delivered in a chaotic way on Saturday. We started the day with Michigan taking down No. 11 Oklahoma in the Big House, and ended it with No. 5 Texas pulling-off a 20-point comeback to shock No. 1 Ohio State in what might turn out to be one of the wildest fourth quarters we witness this season. ARCH MANNING AND TEXAS LONGHORNS ERASE 20-POINT DEFICIT TO STUN OHIO STATE IN SHOCKING COMEBACK FOR THE AGES But, in the middle of what was a remarkable day in the sport, Oklahoma State decided to create pure madness in Stillwater in their win over No. 6 Oregon that sent shockwaves through the college football world. Look, we knew it was going to get a little wild this season. But, the Ducks falling this early in the season, to the Cowboys? This turned out to be a rough day for the Big Ten conference, even with Michigan taking down the Sooners in Ann Arbor. You know, just how we thought it would go, right? No. What are we doing here, Oregon and Ohio State? I've seen a collapse before, but what we witnessed on Saturday night in Austin, Texas, was shocking. The Buckeyes held a 23-3 lead entering the fourth quarter, and everything we had seen up until that point had Ryan Day heading back to Columbus with a monster win. But, it turns out the football gods had other plans for everyone either watching inside DKR Stadium or at home. It was Arch Manning that led a struggling Texas offense from the ashes, just after the internal speaker system finished playing 'Dont Stop Believing' throughout the stadium. I guess this wasn’t the cheesy moment those within the pressbox thought it would turn out to be. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! All it took was for the Longhorns to somehow slow down Jeremiah Smith just enough for them to start putting together enough momentum to steal this one from the Buckeyes. Manning led Texas to three drives that spanned over 10 plays each for touchdowns, sending Ohio State fans who made the trip into a state of shock. "I had nightmares about that game," Arch Manning said after leading his team to the comeback win about last year's game. This one will obviously be remembered for a very long time, especially within the Texas fan base. Just when you thought the Longhorns were buried, somehow these Longhorns found a way to steal one from the Buckeyes. As for Oregon, I have no idea how Dan Lanning explains this one. Oklahoma State had lost 21-straight games to FBS opponents. OKLAHOMA STATE STUNS OREGON, DEALS EARLY SEASON BLOW TO DUCKS' NATIONAL TITLE HOPES This is the same Oklahoma State team that lost to Tulsa last weekend, with new head coach Eric Morris getting the biggest win of his career so far. For the Ducks, losing 39-31 is one thing, but folks should also remember this Oregon team scored fourteen of their points off turnovers. So, it's not as if Dan Lanning's team was flying around all afternoon in Stillwater. An expensive roster can’t save you if the team is not fully prepared for every game. On Saturday, the Oregon Ducks found out the hard way, and now we can throw out all Big Ten predictions in the process. Next week is going to be a movie in Oxford Prepare yourself now, because the next six days are going to center around Lane Kiffin making his return to Ole Miss with his LSU Tigers. Sure, we've got SMU vs. Louisville, Houston versus Texas Tech, along with a few other intriguing matchups. But nothing will touch the cinema that will take place in Oxford, Mississippi. There will be hatred, language, non-stop security surrounding Kiffin as he roams the LSU sidelines, and we still haven’t discussed everything that will encompass next week in the SEC. We've waited almost ten months for Kiffin's return to Ole Miss, which was discussed on what felt like a daily basis during the offseason. Now, we are here. The spotlight is finally shining on what should be the wildest college football environment we see this season, for all the insane reasons you might imagine. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP I know you've been waiting, Ole Miss fans. Your former coach is headed back to town, and all eyes are on this family reunion in Mississippi.

articles.title: PM Modi held 15 bilaterals on sidelines of Brics in 3-day diplomatic marathon
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held 15 sit-down bilateral meetings with heads of state and government over three days on the sidelines of the.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held 15 sit-down bilateral meetings with heads of state and government over three days on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi, in addition to several pull-aside interactions with world leaders and leaders of international institutions, sources told TOI.The packed diplomatic schedule brought PM Modi into direct engagement with leaders from Russia, China, Iran, Africa, Southeast Asia, the Gulf and other regions. The discussions covered bilateral ties, trade, investment, defence, energy, technology, connectivity, critical minerals and major regional and global developments.The engagements took place as India hosted the Brics Summit under its 2026 chairship, with the expanded grouping bringing together countries with differing geopolitical positions. The bilateral meetings provided New Delhi an opportunity to advance its own strategic and economic priorities alongside the broader summit agenda.Also check: 'Thank you for making New Delhi Summit a success'- PM Modi's Brics 2026 closing addressDay 1: Putin, Pezeshkian and UN chiefOn September 11, PM Modi held separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.The Modi-Putin meeting focused on the India-Russia strategic partnership, with the two leaders reviewing cooperation across defence, energy, trade, infrastructure, technology, critical minerals and civil nuclear energy. They also discussed the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the West Asia situation and their impact on maritime trade and the safety of Indian seafarers.PM Modi reiterated India's position that dialogue and diplomacy remained the way forward for resolving conflicts. The two sides also discussed efforts to increase bilateral trade to $100 billion by 2030.PM Modi also met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with the discussions covering India-Iran relations, Brics cooperation and developments in West Asia. PM Modi reiterated India's support for dialogue and diplomacy and stressed the importance of lasting peace and stability in the region.On the same day, PM Modi met UN Secretary-General António Guterres, adding a multilateral dimension to his diplomatic engagements.Day 2: Xi meeting takes centre stageOn September 12, PM Modi held bilateral meetings with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Vietnamese leadership and Chinese President Xi Jinping.The meeting with Xi was among the most closely watched engagements of the summit. The two leaders discussed the India-China relationship, the boundary question, peace and tranquillity along the border, economic and trade ties, supply chains and people-to-people exchanges.PM Modi stressed that differences should not become disputes and underlined the importance of mutual respect, sensitivity and interest in guiding bilateral relations.The meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim covered areas including trade, investment, defence, semiconductors, infrastructure, the digital economy, energy and fintech.PM Modi's meeting with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation and India's engagement with Africa.He also held talks with UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with discussions centred on the India-UAE strategic partnership and cooperation in areas including defence, technology, energy, critical minerals and connectivity.Day 3: Africa, Central Asia and Southeast AsiaOn September 13, PM Modi held bilateral meetings with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Burundian President Evariste Ndayishimiye.He also held engagements with the leadership of Uganda and Nigeria, according to the schedule of bilateral meetings.The meetings broadened India's diplomatic outreach across Africa, Central Asia and Southeast Asia, with discussions focused on strengthening bilateral partnerships and expanding cooperation in areas of mutual interest.The engagement with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa was particularly relevant to the Brics grouping, as South Africa is one of the founding members of the expanded bloc and an important partner for India in advancing the interests of the Global South.The meetings with Egypt and Burundi further strengthened India's engagement with African partners, while the talks with Kazakhstan expanded India's outreach in Central Asia.The Philippines engagement added another important Southeast Asian dimension to PM Modi's diplomatic schedule, alongside his earlier meeting with Malaysia.Bilaterals beyond formal summit agendaThe 15 formal sit-down meetings were accompanied by several shorter pull-aside interactions with other visiting leaders and representatives of international institutions.The diplomatic activity underlined the importance India attached to bilateral engagement during its Brics chairship. While the summit provided a platform for collective discussions among the expanded grouping, the sidelines allowed PM Modi to address country-specific priorities directly with individual leaders.The meetings also came at a time of heightened geopolitical uncertainty, with conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine affecting energy markets, maritime trade and global supply chains.For New Delhi, the three-day diplomatic marathon offered an opportunity to simultaneously deepen strategic partnerships with Russia and the Gulf, stabilise ties with China, maintain engagement with Iran and strengthen India's outreach to Africa, Central Asia and Southeast Asia.The 15 sit-down bilaterals, combined with the additional pull-aside meetings, therefore formed a significant part of PM Modi's diplomatic outreach during India's 2026 Brics chairship.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Modi-Xi's Ukraine offer to Putin, strong message to West & new Brics playbook: Key outcomes of summit
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi brought together leaders of the expanded 11-member grouping for two days of high-level diplomacy, with P.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi brought together leaders of the expanded 11-member grouping for two days of high-level diplomacy, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi holding key bilateral meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.The summit saw a renewed push to stabilise India-China ties, a reaffirmation of the India-Russia strategic partnership and discussions on the West Asia crisis, Ukraine, maritime security, trade and energy. Alongside formal negotiations, images of PM Modi with Xi, Putin and Pezeshkian projected a strong message of engagement and unity within the expanded grouping.The summit also featured informal diplomatic moments, including PM Modi and Putin travelling together by car inside the Bharat Mandapam complex, leaders attending a gala dinner featuring a specially curated Indian menu, and a symbolic Banyan tree plantation highlighting India's emphasis on sustainability and interconnectedness.The two-day summit also produced a series of initiatives covering agriculture, health, technology, startups, energy, urban mobility, supply chains, skilling and global governance. The New Delhi Declaration, adopted after intensive negotiations, provided the summit's principal political outcome, covering terrorism, conflicts, trade, sanctions, energy, finance and development.PM Modi-Xi meeting signals push to stabilise tiesPM Modi and Xi Jinping held a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Brics Summit, with both leaders stressing the need to view India-China relations from a strategic and long-term perspective.The two sides expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question. PM Modi stressed that differences should not become disputes and said the relationship should be guided by mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.The leaders also discussed maintaining peace and tranquillity along the border, economic and trade relations, trade imbalances, supply chains and people-to-people exchanges. Both sides underlined the need to address each other's concerns and facilitate meaningful and predictable market access.Also read: 'Have opportunity to discuss cooperation': PM Modi welcomes Xi; bilateral talks beginPM Modi also thanked China for its support and cooperation during India's Brics chairship and conveyed best wishes to China as it prepares to assume the Brics chairship next year.Xi said China and India should continue to approach their relationship from a strategic perspective and keep long-term bilateral development in mind. He also stressed the importance of cooperation between the two major Global South countries.Modi-Putin talks focus on Ukraine, West AsiaPM Modi and Putin held an over 45-minute bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the summit, reviewing the India-Russia strategic partnership and discussing major regional and global developments.The two leaders discussed the impact of the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the West Asia crisis on maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers. PM Modi reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy remained the way forward in resolving conflicts and said India was ready to assist peace efforts.Also read: Modi-Xi-Putin bonhomie, car diplomacy, gala dinner, Pahalgam condemnation and New Delhi Declaration: Brics Summit key takeawaysThe discussions covered defence, energy, critical minerals, civil nuclear cooperation, fertilisers, infrastructure, technology and industrial cooperation. India and Russia also agreed to work towards increasing bilateral trade to $100 billion by 2030 and discussed implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030.Putin invited PM Modi to Russia for the 24th India-Russia Annual Summit, with dates to be finalised through diplomatic channels.Putin car ride becomes summit highlightOne of the most closely watched visual moments came after the Modi-Putin meeting, when the two leaders travelled together in the same car inside the Bharat Mandapam complex before attending the Brics Business Forum.The image underlined the longstanding India-Russia relationship at a time of continuing geopolitical tensions surrounding Moscow and highlighted India's effort to maintain strategic autonomy.Also read: PM Modi, Putin share car ride again in Delhi, weeks after traveling together in Bishkek - watchPM Modi also presented Putin with a Russian translation of the Thirukkural, the classical Tamil work attributed to poet-saint Thiruvalluvar."Two thousand years ago, Thiruvalluvar wrote the Thirukkural. It includes the entire gamut of human life. It has been translated into the Russian language. I am confident that the people-to-people contact will increase with the translation of the Thirukkural into Russian, which will play a big role in strengthening our relations," Modi told Putin.Kremlin says PM Modi, Xi offered help on UkraineRussia said PM Modi and Xi offered their "good offices" to help find a solution to the Ukraine conflict during their separate interactions with Putin on the sidelines of the summit.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Putin welcomed their readiness, saying: “During their bilateral meetings, Modi and Xi took a keen interest in the Ukraine settlement and actively offered their good offices to help find a solution,”.The development came amid continuing international efforts to find a settlement to the Russia-Ukraine war.PM Modi-Pezeshkian talks centre on West AsiaPM Modi also met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with the discussions focusing on India-Iran ties, Brics cooperation and the escalating conflict in West Asia.PM Modi reiterated India's consistent position that disputes should be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy and stressed the need for lasting peace and stability in the region. The two leaders also discussed freedom of navigation and commerce and the safety and well-being of seafarers amid disruptions to shipping routes.The meeting followed their earlier interaction on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. India has also stressed the need to expand and diversify bilateral trade channels with Iran.Iran-UAE engagement amid regional tensionsPezeshkian also held talks with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the summit.The meeting was significant as Iran and the UAE have had differences over regional security, while Gulf states maintain varying degrees of security cooperation with Western powers.Their interaction highlighted the diplomatic space created by Brics, which brings together countries with competing interests and positions on major geopolitical issues.Modi-Xi-Putin-Pezeshkian project Brics unityThe summit was accompanied by a series of high-profile visuals involving PM Modi, Xi, Putin and Pezeshkian.PM Modi was seen greeting Putin and Xi together, holding their hands and sharing smiles. In another visual, PM Modi walked alongside Putin, Xi and Pezeshkian.PM Modi was also seen holding hands and walking alongside Pezeshkian and other leaders during the Brics Business Forum. The visuals projected unity among members despite differences over conflicts and other major geopolitical issues.The interactions were particularly significant for India as it sought to use its Brics chairship to build consensus among countries with sharply different political and strategic priorities.Also read: PM doubles down on friendship with Iran, seeks win-win strategy; hope mounts for BRICS declarationGala dinner adds cultural dimensionBrics leaders also attended a gala dinner during the summit, providing an informal setting for interaction among heads of state and government.The specially curated Indian menu showcased regional flavours, traditional recipes and contemporary interpretations of Indian cuisine. The menu included Khandvi Mille-Feuille, Khumb Galouti, Paneer Lababdar, Gucchi Marmik, Carrot Bean Poriyal, Thakkali Belle Saaru, Millet Pulao, Beetroot Raita and assorted Indian breads.Desserts included Old Delhi Fruit Cream with Jalebi and Shahtoot Phirni.The cultural evening added a softer dimension to a summit otherwise dominated by negotiations over conflicts, terrorism, trade, energy and global governance.Banyan tree plantation highlights sustainabilityA symbolic Banyan tree plantation ceremony was also held during the summit, with Brics leaders participating in the initiative.The Banyan tree, with its extensive roots and interconnected branches, was presented as a symbol of continuity, resilience and interconnectedness. The gesture complemented India's 2026 Brics theme of "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability".The plantation also reflected India's effort to connect the diplomatic agenda with sustainability and environmental cooperation.Brics Business Forum pushes trade, investmentThe Brics Business Forum brought together heads of state, ministers and business leaders for discussions on trade, investment, finance, technology and development.PM Modi highlighted the economic weight of the expanded grouping, saying Brics countries account for 50 per cent of the world's population, 40 per cent of global GDP and more than 25 per cent of global trade."The growing scale, speed, and optimism of BRICS are clearly evident among us. This forum, hosted in India, is the largest BRICS Business Forum to date,” the Prime Minister said.Pezeshkian called for Brics to convert its economic potential into practical cooperation through trade, investment and joint financing. Putin stressed that business-to-business ties and economic partnerships could help build more resilient international economic relations.PM Modi pushes people-centric BricsIndia's chairship sought to connect Brics cooperation more directly with ordinary citizens while focusing on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability.Addressing the summit, PM Modi said, "It gives me immense pleasure to welcome and greet you all to India. India’s BRICS chairmanship is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach."He said resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability had remained India's priorities, with special emphasis on connecting Brics cooperation with common people."Alongside these priorities, we have placed special emphasis on connecting BRICS cooperation with the common people. With this vision in mind, more than 350 meetings were organised. We had the opportunity to welcome your teams to approximately 30 cities..."India organised more than 350 meetings and high-level engagements across around 30 cities during its 2026 chairship. The programme covered political and security cooperation, economic and financial cooperation, and cultural and people-to-people exchanges.Agriculture and healthcare get major pushBrics countries advanced cooperation in sustainable agriculture through Centres of Excellence on agro-ecology, a Digital Agriculture Network and the Brics AGRIN framework covering agricultural inputs, genetic resources and information.The Digital Agriculture Network is intended to expand the use of AI, geospatial technology, Internet of Things-enabled monitoring and advanced data analytics to support farmers.In healthcare, the Brics Mission for Healthy Lifestyle and a roadmap for joint cooperation on healthy lifestyles were launched. Members also agreed to strengthen cooperation in traditional, complementary and integrative medicine.A greater focus was placed on mental health through the Brics Training Hub Network and Network of Centres of Excellence, with NIMHANS India serving as the coordinating centre.Energy, climate and urban cooperation expandedBrics adopted guiding principles on energy storage and smart grids and launched a Digital Centre of Excellence for Smart Grids and Energy Storage.The grouping also established a Brics Urban Mobility Hub to promote knowledge sharing and technical cooperation on sustainable urban transport. Members adopted voluntary principles on climate-resilient urban infrastructure and established an Urban Research and Knowledge Network.PM Modi also emphasised the importance of balancing development with environmental protection and said technology and critical minerals should not become instruments that hinder shared progress.Startups, MSMEs and skilling receive boostIndia advanced cooperation among small businesses and startups through a Brics MSME Cooperation Portal designed to connect MSMEs, financial institutions, technology centres, trade associations and policymakers.The Brics Incubator Network will connect startups and incubators across member countries, while the Brics Startup Innovation Fund is intended to support early and growth-stage startups.The Brics Science and Research Repository was also welcomed as a platform for scientific knowledge sharing.Through Brics CONNECT, members also advanced cooperation on skills, employability, women's workforce participation, social security and digital public infrastructure.The Brics Youth Cooperation Framework 2026 was adopted to provide greater continuity and structure to youth cooperation, while sports technology cooperation was institutionalised through a dedicated working group.Supply chains and global value chains strengthenedBrics members agreed on a Logistics Supply-Chain Cooperation Framework aimed at improving resilience, sustainability and connectivity.The grouping also advanced cooperation on global value chains through the GVC Action Plan 2026-2030, including a Technical Council and joint study.Members also gave in-principle approval to an agreement on cooperation and mutual administrative assistance in customs matters, aimed at facilitating trade, reducing transaction costs and improving border security and trade facilitation.Global South gets stronger voicePM Modi used the summit to push for greater representation of developing countries in global decision-making institutions.He argued that the Global South should move from being a rule-taker to a rule-shaper and called for reforms in global governance, including greater representation in the UN Security Council.Brics also reaffirmed support for comprehensive UN reform and a more democratic, representative and inclusive international system.China and Russia reiterated support for the aspirations of India and Brazil to play a greater role in the UN, including the Security Council.New Delhi Declaration: 140 points, 45 pagesThe Brics countries adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026, a 45-page document containing 140 points, after intensive negotiations that continued into the early hours of Saturday.The declaration brings together the grouping's positions on terrorism, unilateral military action, West Asia, global governance, trade, sanctions, energy, finance, development and the interests of the Global South.Its adoption was particularly significant because the expanded Brics includes countries with differing positions on major geopolitical conflicts, including Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. India worked to bridge differences and secure consensus among members.Pahalgam attack explicitly condemnedThe declaration strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and called for "zero tolerance for terrorism".It specifically condemned the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terrorist attack, in which 26 people were killed. The declaration also condemned the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens.Brics reaffirmed that terrorism cannot be associated with any religion, nationality, civilisation or ethnic group and called for those involved in terrorist activities and their support to be held accountable.The grouping also called for progress towards adopting the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism under the UN framework.West Asia: Restraint, ceasefire and diplomacyThe declaration expressed deep concern over the continuing escalation in West Asia and called on all parties to exercise maximum restraint.It stressed dialogue, consultation and diplomacy as the means to address conflicts and called for the protection of civilians and humanitarian assistance.On Gaza, Brics called for upholding a ceasefire, ensuring unhindered humanitarian assistance and ending the forced displacement of Palestinians. It reaffirmed support for a two-state solution based on the internationally recognised 1967 borders.Unilateral military action condemnedThe declaration condemned unilateral military action without naming any country.The language assumes significance against the backdrop of ongoing conflicts in West Asia and the wider divisions within the expanded grouping.The consensus was reached after negotiations continued into the early hours of Saturday, with India working to reconcile competing positions and produce a common statement.Trade, tariffs and sanctionsBrics expressed concern over unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that distort international trade and create uncertainty for businesses and supply chains.The grouping reaffirmed support for a rules-based multilateral trading system centred on the World Trade Organization and called for restoration of a fully functioning two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism.Brics also voiced opposition to unilateral coercive measures that it considers inconsistent with international law and the principles of the UN Charter, calling for such measures to be eliminated.Local currencies and financial resilienceThe declaration backed efforts to promote cross-border payments and trade settlements using Brics members' local currencies while respecting national priorities.Members acknowledged work on the interoperability of payment and messaging systems and discussions on facilitating trade settlements and investment using local currencies.The push forms part of a broader effort to strengthen financial resilience and reduce vulnerabilities in international economic relations.Critical minerals and energy securityThe declaration stressed the importance of reliable, diversified, resilient and sustainable supply chains for critical minerals.It called for benefit sharing, value addition and economic diversification in resource-rich countries while recognising their sovereign rights over mineral resources.Brics also stressed the importance of critical minerals for zero and low-emission technologies, energy security and resilient energy supply chains.On energy, the declaration called for diversified sources, resilient infrastructure and stable markets. It recognised that fossil fuels would continue to play an important role, particularly for emerging and developing economies, while backing equitable and inclusive energy transitions.Health and universal health coverageThe declaration reaffirmed Brics' commitment to universal health coverage and resilient, inclusive and people-centred health systems.Members emphasised the coordinating role of the World Health Organisation and backed continued multilateral cooperation on global health.The declaration also covered the Pandemic Agreement's Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing negotiations, efforts to end tuberculosis, strengthening the health workforce, digital health and integration of traditional medicine.Women, development and global governanceBrics recognised women as leaders, decision-makers and drivers of economic growth and social transformation.The declaration stressed women's participation in governance and economic life, financial and digital inclusion, skill development, entrepreneurship and climate action.The grouping also reaffirmed the importance of reforming global institutions to reflect contemporary economic and political realities and strengthen the voice of developing countries.A wider Brics enters its third decadeThe New Delhi Summit came as Brics entered its third decade with 11 full members: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the UAE.India's 2026 chairship was its fourth after previous presidencies in 2012, 2016 and 2021. The latest chairship sought to build on those earlier efforts while adapting the grouping's agenda to its expanded membership.In his concluding remarks, PM Modi said the discussions had strengthened the view that Brics had evolved beyond a traditional grouping and could function as an ecosystem for practical solutions."Our discussions over the past two days have further strengthened our conviction that BRICS is not merely a grouping of nations, but an ecosystem of solutions. We hope that the New Delhi Declaration adopted at this summit will provide a clear direction for our shared vision and future cooperation. We must translate all outcomes into time-bound actions that deliver last-mile impact. We will work together to ensure that our framework moves beyond mere documentation and creates a tangible impact in real life," he said.PM Modi also said the world now expected concrete results from Brics rather than only ideas and commitments, as the grouping prepares to enter its third decade.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
